findings.evidence: grep: Mathlib `Orthogonality.lean:67` has `theorem integrable_measureT {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc (-1) 1)) : Integrable f measureT`; PR line 162 states exactly the specialization to a continuous exponential-absolute function.
findings.fix: Remove this lemma or make downstream code use `integrable_measureT (by fun_prop)` directly.
findings.issue: `integrable_exp_abs_measureT` duplicates the existing generic Mathlib theorem `Polynomial.Chebyshev.integrable_measureT` specialized to the continuous function `fun x => Real.exp (a * |x|)`.

findings.evidence: grep: Mathlib `Orthogonality.lean:67` provides `integrable_measureT`; Mathlib `Integrable.lean:1107` provides `Integrable.ofReal`; PR lines 168-172 are only this specialization plus `.ofReal`.
findings.fix: Remove this lemma or inline `(integrable_measureT (by fun_prop : ContinuousOn (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (a * |x|)) (Set.Icc (-1) 1))).ofReal (𝕜 := 𝕜)` at the use site.
findings.issue: `integrable_algebraMap_exp_abs_measureT` is the same redundant specialization after scalar cast: prove the real case with `integrable_measureT (by fun_prop)` and apply `.ofReal`.

summary: The new exponential-moment consumer lemmas are just special cases of Mathlib's existing Chebyshev integrability theorem, so this PR adds redundant API instead of reusing the located replacement.
